newsitem.title: BELGIUM: NATO discusses new links with Russia.
newsitem.headline: NATO discusses new links with Russia.

text.p: NATO countries on Thursday examined proposals for a special charter with Russia taking in all aspects of relations between the two former Cold War foes, alliance sources said.
They said NATO's 16 ambassadors exchanged views on the exact shape any future relationship should take as part of efforts to inaugurate a new era of close cooperation.
"The allies are all keen on trying to set up some form of mechanism that allows Moscow to have some form of hot-line in NATO headquarters," said one senior diplomat.
No decisions were taken at the informal meeting, but sources said the ambassadors would return to the subject in formal session over the next few weeks.

NATO has offered Russia an enhanced relationship, but Moscow wants this enshrined in a treaty or charter taking account of its weight in world affairs and distinguishing it from the alliance's links with other former communist states.

Last week, German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said in a newspaper article the West would do its best to put relations with Russia on a firmer footing and said he was confident Moscow would take up an offer of cooperation with NATO.

Kinkel, writing in the Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung newspaper, said the West still faced uncertainties in dealing with Russia, concerning the stability of its democracy and the health of President Boris Yeltsin.
